svg.text: Two Rock Classic Reverb Signature 100 — RECONSTRUCTED topology used by the DSP model
Two Rock has not published a schematic. This is a Fender-derived reconstruction with a Dumble-style stack, master volume, presence and tube-rectifier supply.
BRIGHT switch: HF shelf before V1A (+6 dB > 1.8 kHz)
Guitar source ≈30k; 68k stopper; Miller C ≈100pF rolls off the top.
② TMB tone stack (exactly the topology the DSP solves)
Insertion loss ≈ -17 dB at the mids with all knobs at 10; deeper scoop as MID is lowered.
Reconstruction values — edit in AmpCore.h to taste.
③ Volume and V1B gain stage
10k audio pot; sets power-stage drive independent of preamp gain
④ Phase inverter, 4×6L6GC output stage, output transformer, NFB + PRESENCE
4×6L6GC (two per side), tube rectifier = more sag, fixed bias. No tremolo on this voicing.
Output transformer centre-tap B+: 470 V (GZ34 rectifier)
